title: Ask sets up the house, and Kitchen is part of Ask
changes: Ask can change how Home Assistant is set up: move a light to another room, rename it, add or remove a room, change a scene, make an automation or switch one off, set the thermostat, lock a door.
It does these at once and says so in a sentence, with Undo under the answer, on Activity and on Changes, for a day.
Anything that removes something, unlocking or opening a door, and settings for the whole house wait on a card for your tap. Typing yes does nothing.

Kitchen is part of Ask. Say “add sponges and two avocados to the list” and Hub picks the exact product you buy, from your past orders. What you have never bought waits for one pick, and Hub knows it next time.
The Kitchen screen is the list on its way into the cart: each thing, its product, where it stands, and what needs you. Recipes and the order to place are drawn in Ask, under what you asked.
With “Fill the cart by itself” switched on, what you add in Ask, on the screen or on your Groceries reminders lands in the cart a minute later. Placing an order still takes your tap.
The list needs the kitchen service’s own update. Until it has it, Kitchen still answers in words.

title: Everything that happened in the house
changes: Activity, under System, lists what happened in the house, newest first: lights, doors and locks, button presses, automations and music, from Home Assistant, Apple Home and Hub itself.
Each line says what did it when that's known: a person, an automation, or Hub with Undo. Apple Home never says who, so its lines don't either.
A device that both Home Assistant and Apple Home report shows once, and Hub keeps 90 days, longer than Home Assistant does.
Motion and everything else are a tap away, and the list can be narrowed to one source.

title: Music in another room, and every screen in the app
changes: Music in another room is one tap: the music sheet lists every room, and a quiet one has Play here, for music of its own that starts softly while the rest plays on, and Join.
A room's own panel offers the same, the bar at the bottom names rooms playing something else, and a room playing its own music has its own pause.
Deploy is in the app: Versions shows a new version with a Deploy button, says when Hub is updating, and reloads by itself when the new version runs.
Engine is a screen in the app: what you asked Hub for, notes and routines waiting for a tap, how far Hub may go, and what the models cost.
Mail's Rules and settings open in the app: the plan with Apply and Undo, how far Hub files each kind, the charge alert and the 30-day rules.
Everything Hub changed, in the house and in playlists, is a screen in the app, each change with Undo for a day.
The older pages wear the app's look and carry its tabs, so none of them looks or feels like the old Hub.

title: Buttons on the wall show in their room
changes: A wall or remote button shows in its room, with its last press, its battery and what each press does.
The developer page reads the projects folder, and shows its tmux and brief sections only when they are set.

title: The app becomes Hub's front door, with Mail and Kitchen
changes: Hub's usual address opens the new app. The older pages stay under System, and the old chat is at /ask.
A Versions page under System lists each release with what changed and links to the code.
Mail is a screen in the app: what needs you and who hasn't answered, then what Hub sorted, with filing and Undo.
Kitchen is a screen in the app: the conversation, recipes, cart plans, orders and the shopping list.
Ask can now read your mail, calendar and school details on Claude Sonnet to answer questions about your day.

title: The new app: Home, Music, Ask and Today
changes: The new app at /app: the house as a plan of rooms that light up, with music, scenes and Undo.
Ask inside the app, on Claude Sonnet, for requests about the house: say it and Hub does it.
Today inside the app: what needs you first, then the rest of the day.

title: Dev page fix
changes: The Dev page reads terminal window names that contain spaces.

title: Home Assistant inside Hub, and live checks
changes: Home Assistant and Music Assistant open inside Hub, behind Hub's sign-in.
Live checks: small tests of the real running system that a deploy must pass.
A Dev page with every project's live state.
Silent speakers fold under one line on the Music screen.

title: Ask plays the music it found
changes: When Ask finds music, it plays it instead of only naming it.

title: Ask lists the devices on the network
changes: Ask can list the devices on the home network, grouped by mesh unit.

title: Today's Home card leads to Music
changes: The Home card on Today leads to Music and Music Assistant.

title: A mini-player and a Music screen
changes: A mini-player on Hub's pages while music plays, and a Music screen under Home.

title: Rooms from Home Assistant, and a Now playing card
changes: Rooms come from Home Assistant's areas and labels, and light colours stay within bounds.
Ask shows a live Now playing card.
Home Assistant and Music Assistant are one tap away.

title: Hub gets a logo
changes: A logo, with every icon drawn from it. The empty Ask chat shows it.

title: A record of every Ask turn
changes: Each Ask turn is recorded, failed answers included, with an Ask activity page to look back at them.
Music plays only real items, checks that it started, and groups under the speaker already playing.

title: A new look
changes: A warm paper palette, raised cards, pill buttons and a segmented main menu.
A calmer Ask chat with a floating box to type in.
Icons on every tool, and charts on the new palette.

title: Cards in the chat, recipes and fix cards
changes: Ask shows cards in the chat, with an Improve this button.
Saved routines (recipes) of allowed steps, kept only when you tap to save.
"As well" plays music in sync across speakers.
A friction log, and morning cards offering fixes: Build, Not now or Never.
When a name is both a room and a device, Hub takes it to mean the room.

title: Ask plays music where asked
changes: Ask plays a specific pick, only on the speakers asked for, and softly when asked.

title: Playlists through Music Assistant
changes: Hub can make and change playlists in Music Assistant, with Undo and reminders.
Each background playlist edit is checked before the next one starts.

title: Hub can run the house
changes: Hub reads the house through Home Assistant and can change lights, plugs, scenes and speakers, with Undo.
Mail filing and pause say plainly what they did; Calendar shows several days; Bike + bus is sturdier.
Hub's database is created readable by the owner only.

title: Ask hands cooking and groceries to Kitchen
changes: Ask passes cooking and grocery requests to Kitchen, and Kitchen's cards show in the chat.
A preview Hub for development, on a copy of real data.

title: Three main views: Ask, Today and Insights
changes: Hub's top bar settles on three views: Ask, Today and Insights.
Ask can look up the network, the inbox's size and what the AI has cost.
Insights gains a network summary; Today stops showing a second card for a tool that already asks for a decision.
Trip starts from a made-up sample trip and always keeps the saved one exactly as it was.
An attempt the night before rolled itself back; this release carries the same changes.

title: Ask Hub, a chat that can look things up
changes: Ask Hub: a chat that answers from Hub's own lookups. It can read, not change.
The first release from the cleaned-up history; the source is ready to be public.
